title: Bijectivity of the normalized diagonal comparison on an affine chart
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], let $C$ be its diagonal conormal [def-sc-diagonal-conormal], and let $D:\mathcal O_X\to C$ be any relative derivation satisfying the normalization in [lem-sc-diagonal-conormal-derivation-exists]. Let $\phi:\Omega_{X/S}\to C$ be the map corresponding to $D$ under the universal property of relative differentials [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf]. For every affine open $U\subset X$ and affine open $V\subset S$ with $U\subset f^{-1}V$, the map $\Gamma(U,\phi)$ is bijective. The statement concerns one affine chart; it asserts neither existence of $D$ nor a global isomorphism.

proof.text: Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ with the ring map supplied by $f$. The open $U\times_V U$ in the product is $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R A)$ and its diagonal inverse image is $U$ (Tag 01KJ). The restricted actual kernel is the ideal of its closed diagonal, namely the kernel $J$ of multiplication. Open restriction of this kernel and of tensor pullback gives the conormal of that affine closed immersion. The affine conormal sections theorem identifies its sections with $J/J^2$ including the class map of the tensor-pullback unit.

The already-proved relativeDifferentialsRestrictIso, relativeDifferentialsCompIso and relativeDifferentialsSpecIso identify differential sections on $U$ with $\Omega_{A/R}$ and preserve the differential formula. The normalization of $D$ and relativeDifferentialsHomEquiv_symm_app_d identify the map on $da$ with the class of $1\otimes a-a\otimes1$. These $da$ span $\Omega_{A/R}$. By the ring-level diagonal cotangent identification, this is the canonical isomorphism $\Omega_{A/R}\cong J/J^2$. Conjugate it by the section identifications to deduce bijectivity.
